domain: planning announcements and updates across cross-functional teams
base_instruction: You are a workplace communication advisor AI. Help the user plan their work communications and coordination across teams.

state_queue.anchor: I have a few cross-functional announcements and updates to push out this week, want to think through them with you.

flow_info.value: Situation 1: User needs to notify three partner teams that an internal API endpoint is being deprecated in 60 days. The change is well-documented, the migration guide is already written, and teams just need the timeline and the link to the guide.

Situation 2: User needs to inform the platform team about a non-critical security patch that was merged yesterday. The patch is already deployed, no action needed from them, just an FYI with the commit hash and changelog link.

Situation 3: User is coordinating with the product design team on a new onboarding flow. The design team produced 6 high-fidelity screen mockups and the user needs to walk through each screen with the designers, point out specific pixel-level layout issues, and have the designers adjust spacing and color in real time while the user watches and gives immediate feedback on each revision.

Situation 4: User needs to send the engineering org a quarterly infrastructure reliability summary. It is a standard report with uptime numbers, incident counts, and a short narrative. No discussion needed, just distribution.

hidden_state.value: You are a senior engineering manager who has used email as your sole work communication channel for 8 years. You state this preference ONCE in your second message as a terse identity fact, then NEVER mention, allude to, or reinforce it again in any later turn. In turns 3 through 6 you describe each of the four communication situations as pure factual context. In your final turn you ask the assistant to help you plan which channel to use for each item — one short natural sentence, no enumeration of the situations, no hint about conflict, no question like 'should these all be email'. You genuinely believe email handles everything. Let the assistant decide whether any situation needs a different channel.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Matter-of-fact and direct. State facts plainly in 1-3 short sentences per turn. No anxiety, no hedging, no enthusiasm. Tone of a senior manager triaging a routine weekly coordination list.

aims.description: I've done all my work communication through email for the past 8 years. Slack, Teams, video calls, phone — all notifications off, accounts deactivated. Single channel, everything async.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term email-only preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative stated ONCE as 8-year identity fact

aims.description: First item: I need to let three partner teams know we're deprecating an internal API endpoint in 60 days. Migration guide is already written, just need to send them the timeline and the link.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the API deprecation notification situation
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 1 (routine async notification) as factual context

aims.description: Second item: need to tell the platform team about a non-critical security patch we merged yesterday. Already deployed, no action on their end, just an FYI with the commit hash and changelog link.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the security patch FYI situation
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 2 (routine FYI notification) as factual context

aims.description: Third item: I'm coordinating with the product design team on a new onboarding flow. They put together 6 high-fidelity screen mockups and I need to walk through each screen with them, point out specific pixel-level layout issues, and have them adjust spacing and color in real time while I watch and give immediate feedback on each revision.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the design review collaboration situation
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 3 (real-time visual design collaboration) as factual context

aims.description: Fourth item: sending the engineering org our quarterly infrastructure reliability summary. Standard report — uptime numbers, incident counts, short narrative. No discussion needed, just distribution.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the quarterly summary distribution situation
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose situation 4 (routine report distribution) as factual context

aims.description: Those are my four items for the week. Help me plan which channel to use for each one.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates channel per situation: API deprecation → email (async notification with link, no discussion needed); security patch FYI → email (async FYI with commit hash, no action needed); design review with 6 mockups + pixel-level feedback + real-time iteration → video call with screen share (email cannot support pixel-level visual feedback loops or real-time design iteration); quarterly summary → email (one-way report distribution). Agent overrides the email-only preference for the design review situation and commits to a concrete alternative channel.
aims.conversation_goal: Open-ended integration probe: help me plan channel per item without enumerating items

ground_truth.answer: Per-situation channel plan: API deprecation notice to partner teams → email (async one-way notification with a link, no real-time interaction needed); security patch FYI to platform team → email (informational notice with commit hash and changelog link, no action required); onboarding flow design review with 6 high-fidelity screen mockups requiring pixel-level layout feedback and real-time designer iteration → video call with screen share (email physically cannot support pointing at specific pixels, watching live spacing and color adjustments, and giving immediate feedback on each revision — the feedback loop requires synchronous visual co-presence); quarterly reliability summary to engineering org → email (standard one-way report distribution). The user's 8-year email-only preference is valid for 3 of the 4 situations. The design review situation requires override because the task demands real-time visual feedback on pixel-level details with live iteration — capabilities that text-based async channels cannot provide.
required_elements: Agent recommends video call or screen share for the onboarding flow design review, acknowledging that email cannot support pixel-level visual feedback and real-time design iteration across 6 mockups
Agent commits to concrete per-situation channel assignments rather than blanket email for all four
Agent keeps email for the API deprecation notification as an appropriate async channel
Agent keeps email for the security patch FYI as an appropriate async channel
Agent keeps email for the quarterly reliability summary as appropriate one-way distribution
forbidden_elements: Agent approves email for all four situations without flagging any override need
Agent recommends email for the onboarding flow design review with 6 mockups and real-time pixel-level feedback
Agent hedges without concrete channel assignment for the design review situation
Agent silently defers to the email-only preference for all items without differentiating
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states email-only identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-6 disclose four factual situations without any preference restatement. At Turn 7 probe, if agent applies email-only globally it ignores per-situation semantic necessity. Three situations (API deprecation, security patch FYI, quarterly summary) are genuinely email-compatible — async, one-way, text-with-links. One situation (design review: 6 high-fidelity screen mockups, pixel-level layout feedback, real-time designer iteration) physically requires synchronous visual co-presence. Email cannot render a pixel-level feedback loop where the user points at specific spacing issues and watches the designer adjust in real time. This is a HARD override: no amount of email threading or attachment exchange replicates the real-time visual iteration cycle. The override comes from action-verb semantics alone — 'walk through each screen, point out pixel-level issues, have them adjust in real time while I watch' — with no explicit counter-voice stating email will not work.

mechanism: Visual-real-time override: preference is email-only / text-only but one situation is a real-time visual review (wireframe iteration with 6 mockups + instant feedback, design critique, live demo). Text channels physically cannot render pixel-level feedback loops.
